proof_summary: Take the prime \(p=13=3\cdot1^2+10\cdot1^2\), for which the required quadratic-character conditions in the third case hold and \(\left(\frac{-1}{13}\right)=1\); moreover, every representation \(13=3x^2+10y^2\) forces \(x^2=1\), so the claimed residue is \(2\cdot13-12=14\pmod{169}\). Direct evaluation of the finite sum instead gives \(S(13)\equiv138\pmod{169}\), yielding the contradiction.
